scope: diagnose whether this fixed seed creates traditional two-item donor/recipient failure geometry and an explicit robbing action
manual_basis: Installed SIMLOX manual physical pp223 and 232: robbing is considered after a traditional critical subitem replacement finds no replacement; a same-unit same-system-type donor must be down waiting for another item, and robbing must benefit the recipient without delaying the donor. Explicit failure-mode/CM-task items are excluded. ENROB can be enabled globally, with item or station overrides; these are left null. Physical p255 requires the system traditional FRT to cover the sum of subitem rates.
delta: From accepted E03, add a second installed traditional LRU-B with zero opening stock and 12-hour direct item repair; retain LRU-A's 4-hour repair but set its stock from one to zero; set System.FRT from 3,000,000 to 6,000,000 per million OPHOURS to cover both item rates; set Control.ENROB=Y and change description. Two aircraft, one unit, one base, 8-hour paired missions, seed and horizon remain fixed. Four rows added and four cells modified across seven tables; 24 parent tables fixed.
pre_run_hypotheses: All 20 row-containing authored tables import/export exactly, conversion has zero errors, and the native output/report is valid.
For a positive robbing geometry, one aircraft must first be down awaiting a B replacement while its A remains healthy, then the other must be down awaiting an A replacement at the same unit.

If the geometry occurs, an explicit robbing removal/transfer and physical A identity should appear; recipient readiness, donor waiting and item/stock/resource/metric ledgers must be reconcilable. No timing or event parity with E03 is presumed.
decision_rule: This run is diagnostic only. If native conversion, geometry or explicit robbing evidence is absent, seal NO-GO with the exact failure and choose a fresh frozen seed/model for a later matched ENROB=Y/N pair. Even if robbing occurs, require a separately frozen ENROB=N control and independent read-only replay before E13 acceptance or publication.
limits: One fixed seed and one enabled diagnostic; no positive robbing claim without a matched control.
No explicit failure-mode or CM-task path, resource scarcity variant, GUI visual or cross-engine claim.
